findings.explanation: google_project_iam_policy writes the whole project policy, auditConfigs included, and the provider documents that it fights google_project_iam_audit_config. data.google_iam_policy.project only emits binding blocks, so enabling var.project_bindings silently deletes every Data Access audit log setting on the project and there is no way to pass them through the module. No holden policy checks the policy_data source for audit_config on an authoritative project policy. Medium confidence because the impact depends on what audit configs the project currently has.
findings.remediation: Add an optional var.project_audit_configs and render it as dynamic audit_config blocks in data.google_iam_policy.project; document that it is part of the complete policy.
findings.resolution_note: Fixed: added var.project_audit_configs, rendered as dynamic audit_config blocks in data.google_iam_policy.project, and documented in the README that unlisted audit configs are removed.
findings.title: Project IAM policy is built with no audit_config, so applying it wipes the project's Data Access audit log configuration

findings.explanation: var.project defaults to "" and its validation accepts the empty string, but nothing ties it to var.project_bindings. A caller who sets the bindings and forgets the project gets an apply-time API error (best-fit principle: the apply fails). The module's README promises the dangerous resource is guarded at input time.
findings.remediation: Add a lifecycle precondition on google_project_iam_policy.project requiring var.project to be non-empty (preconditions work on tofu >= 1.2, unlike cross-variable validation).
findings.resolution_note: Fixed: lifecycle precondition on google_project_iam_policy.project requires var.project when var.project_bindings is set.
findings.title: Setting var.project_bindings without var.project passes an empty project ID to google_project_iam_policy

findings.explanation: The validation only checks that some binding has role roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin; a binding with members = [] satisfies it, and the applied policy then leaves nobody able to change project IAM, which is exactly the lockout the validation's error message says it prevents.
findings.fix: condition = length(var.project_bindings) == 0 || anytrue([for b in var.project_bindings : b.role == "roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin" && length(b.members) > 0])
findings.remediation: Require the projectIamAdmin binding to have at least one member.
findings.resolution_note: Fixed: the projectIamAdmin lockout validation now also requires at least one member.
findings.title: Lockout guard on var.project_bindings accepts a projectIamAdmin binding with no members

findings.explanation: default_table_expiration_ms and default_partition_expiration_ms are both set from var.default_table_expiration_ms (default 7776000000, 90 days). A module whose purpose is IAM ownership therefore also expires whole tables 90 days after creation by default, and a caller cannot keep tables while expiring old partitions. Medium confidence: the variable description does state it covers both.
findings.remediation: Split into separate table and partition expiration variables and consider a null (no expiry) default for tables.
findings.resolution_note: Fixed (breaking): default_partition_expiration_ms is now driven by a new variable var.default_partition_expiration_ms, and both var.default_table_expiration_ms and var.default_partition_expiration_ms default to null (no expiry). Existing deployments that relied on the previous 90-day default will have table and partition expiry removed on next apply unless they set the variables explicitly. HLD_GCP_173 (dataset must set a default table expiration) is suppressed inline with the justification that retention is the caller's decision.
findings.title: One variable drives both table and partition expiration, and its default deletes every table in the dataset after 90 days

suggested_policies.rationale: An authoritative google_project_iam_policy replaces the project's auditConfigs as well as its bindings. When the referenced data.google_iam_policy has no audit_config block, applying it removes Data Access audit logging. Concrete, resource-type-scoped and applies to any Terraform using these types; no built-in policy covers it (HLD_GCP_305/379 cover primitive roles and use of the resource, not audit config loss).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_001
name: google_project_iam_policy must carry audit_config in its policy data
principle: logging-and-monitoring
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  google_project_iam_policy writes the entire project IAM policy, including
  auditConfigs. If the data.google_iam_policy it is built from has no
  audit_config block, every Data Access audit log configuration on the
  project is deleted on apply, and it conflicts with any
  google_project_iam_audit_config managed elsewhere.
message: |
  google_project_iam_policy.policy_data comes from a data.google_iam_policy
  with no audit_config block; applying it removes the project's audit configs.
remediation: |
  Add audit_config blocks to the data.google_iam_policy (for example
  service = "allServices" with DATA_READ, DATA_WRITE and ADMIN_READ log
  types), or use additive google_project_iam_member resources instead.
resources:
  google_project_iam_policy:
    references:
      via: policy_data
      type: data.google_iam_policy
      must:
        path: audit_config
        not_null: true
